Turner oṣati explicitly records Khowar uṣák cold beside Dameli oṣé- to be frostbitten. The survey uṣak forms match that cited Khowar word. The apparently unusual burn/cold semantic history is Turner’s explicit comparison, not an inferred equation with warm uṣṇa.

Turner avaśyā/avaśyāya explicitly records Kalasha oš ice/cold, alongside the wider dew/frost family. These Kalasha cold responses match that exact comparandum; they are kept separate from Khowar uṣák under oṣati.

Turner karkara explicitly gives Oriya kākara dew and Punjabi/Lahnda kakkar frost. These eastern kākər/kakor cold responses are compared with that documented dew/frost family, preserving the survey’s adjectival cold use and local vowels. The semantic extension is regional and does not imply a claim about every individual consonant change.

Turner śītala explicitly gives Gujarati śīḷũ cold/stale and Marathi śiḷā cold/stale. These Mewari hīl-/hīr- cold forms are qualified regional comparisons with that ī-vowel family, including s/h and l/r variation; the competing e-vowel śaitala family is not merged into this group.
